why_that_detail_means_the_writes_worked: The bench returns 'model wrote N file(s)' if writes < 2, and 'malformed tool call refused' if a later round broke the parse. The recorded detail is specifically 'model did not call pytest', so the model emitted at least two well-formed write calls and then stopped.
root_cause: Planning follow-through, not a harness parse/repair issue and not a missing tool. act() feeds tool results back with 'Continue. Emit the next tool_call if more work remains, or reply with plain text if the task is done.' After writing tiny.py and test_tiny.py the model treated the authoring as complete and replied in plain text. The original prompt also said 'Emit one tool_call per action', which forced multi-round instead of using the already-supported multi-block parse.
what_was_not_done: Harness did not inject a pytest call
Scoring was not weakened to write-only
A malformed call was not repaired into pytest
The task was not reclassified as harness-expected
what_changed_after_the_diagnosis: Prompt now requires a pytest tool_call as the last action, allows all three <tool_call> blocks in one reply, and gives five rounds / 384 new tokens. Pass criteria are unchanged: two writes (tiny.py + test_tiny.py) plus a pytest call that succeeds.

after_prompt_change.meaning: The clearer prompt did not produce follow-through. The model wrote tiny.py three times and never authored the test or called pytest. Kept as a FAIL, not weakened.

if_it_still_fails: Keep the FAIL. That is a model-capability finding on multi-step author-then-test, not a reason to shrink the bench.
